title: Will My Architect Work With My Contractor on a Westchester Project?
excerpt: If you already have a contractor for your Westchester renovation or addition, you might wonder if an architect will actually collaborate with them. The short answer is yes, but it depends on who you hire.
content:
When homeowners in towns like Scarsdale and Mamaroneck start planning a renovation or addition, they often ask the same question: can my architect and contractor actually work together, or will they clash over control and money?

It's a fair concern. You've heard stories. But the real answer depends entirely on who you hire first and what their business model actually is.

The Problem With Separate Architects and Contractors

When you hire an architect and a contractor separately, you're creating a relationship that has built-in tension. The architect designs the project. The contractor builds it. If something goes wrong or costs more than expected, each one blames the other. You end up caught in the middle.

This doesn't mean it can't work. It just means you need clear contracts and someone willing to referee. Many homeowners in Bronxville and Pelham Manor do hire separate professionals successfully. But it takes more time to coordinate, more money on both sides, and more stress for you.

Why Design-Build Works Differently

A design-build firm is different. One company handles both the architecture and the construction. That means no finger-pointing. No turf wars. One person takes responsibility for the whole project from drawing board to finished kitchen or second-story addition.

Silvio M. Luca runs House Architecture & Construction as a design-build firm where the principal is both a licensed New York architect and a licensed general contractor. He personally oversees every project in Westchester, whether it's a historic restoration in Tarrytown, a kitchen remodel in Larchmont, or a primary suite addition in White Plains.

When one person carries both licenses and runs the job personally, the architect and contractor aren't two separate entities trying to negotiate. They're the same entity with one reputation on the line.

What This Means for Your Westchester Project

If you're planning a home renovation in Westchester County and you choose a design-build approach, you won't have to wonder if your architect and contractor will get along. You also won't have to shop for both separately or manage two different relationships.

Whether your project is in Harrison, Eastchester, Rye, or Hastings-on-Hudson, every municipality has its own building department and permit process. A design-build firm that knows your local requirements and has worked in your town before moves faster through those steps. There's no back-and-forth between an architect's office and a construction company trying to figure out who's handling the permit application.

This applies to any type of work. Open-concept conversions, kitchen and bathroom renovations, home additions, custom new construction in Westchester County. The advantage stays the same: one vision, one responsibility, one point of contact.

If you already have a contractor and want to bring in a licensed architect in Westchester to handle just the design, that can work too. But your contractor and architect will need to have a professional relationship and clear communication lines. Make sure both are willing to collaborate before you sign anyone.
